STATES: u0, u1, u2, u3
INITIAL_STATE: u0
FINAL_STATES: u3
TRANSITION_FUNCTION:
(u0, box_fell) -> u1
(u0, at_exit) -> u2
(u0, holding_box) -> u0
(u0, else) -> u0
(u1, holding_box) -> u2
(u1, at_exit) -> u2
(u1, else) -> u1
(u2, holding_box) -> u3
(u2, at_exit) -> u2
(u2, else) -> u2
(u3, else) -> u3
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, at_exit, u2) -> 0.2
(u1, holding_box, u2) -> 0.1
(u1, at_exit, u2) -> 0.2
(u2, holding_box, u3) -> 1.0
feedback: Semantic and structural issues reject this candidate. (1) Purpose mismatch / state explosion at the exit: FINAL_STATES lists u3 as the accepting state, but the machine only reaches u3 via (u2, holding_box) → u3, and from u2 it also takes (u2, at_exit) → u2 which pays 0.2. If the agent reaches the exit without the box, it enters u2 and stays there (at_exit repeats while standing on the exit), so the episode ends in a non-accepting final state — that part is consistent with 'you must be carrying the box at the exit'. However the accepting state u3 is reached only at the step the agent is on the exit while holding the box; after the episode ends, u3 is a dead sink. That is workable, but see next issues. (2) The task also demands 'pick the box up again on your very next move' after box_fell, and 'reach the exit carrying the box'. The machine never rewards or even tracks a timely re-pickup beyond one step: (u1, holding_box) → u2 gives +0.1 regardless of whether the pickup happened on the very next move or much later (the else self-loop does not penalize delay), and worse, from u2 further falls are ignored — if the box falls again while in u2 (e.g., after exiting-not, or between picking up and reaching the exit), the machine stays in u2 on else, so a second fall is never required to be recovered. There is no (u2, box_fell) → u1 transition, violating the 'whenever the box falls, pick it up again' obligation for falls occurring after the first recovery. (3) Rewards are bounded and dense-ish, but the (u0, at_exit, u2) → 0.2 transition rewards exiting without the box, contradicting the requirement that exit must happen while carrying the box — reaching the exit bare-handed should yield 0 total, not 0.2. (4) Ordered transition coverage: the first box_fell is covered from u0 only; falls in u1 (can the box fall before it is picked up again? yes, at the scheduled due step) are handled by the else self-loop, which is fine since holding_box → u2 recovers; but the pickup after a fall could occur on the same step only if the fall and pickup coincide — events apply after the action, so pickup followed by fall on the same step leaves holding_box true in the same observation as box_fell; the u0 machine has no transition on {box_fell, holding_box} simultaneous; predicate-only events are declared but the transition table doesn't handle multi-label steps deterministically per the required convention. (5) Irrelevant events (switch_toggled, siren_ringing) are only covered by per-state else self-loops — that is acceptable. (6) The final state u3 has no reward on reaching it via at_exit while already holding — actually (u2, holding_box) → u3 fires while standing on the exit holding, which pays 1.0; ok. But if the agent holds the box the entire episode and reaches the exit without ever a fall (u0, holding_box → u0, then at_exit → u2 pays 0.2, then (u2, holding_box) → u3 pays 1.0), the total is 1.2 — the exit-with-box case pays the same 1.2 whether or not a fall ever happened, and a fall-free episode passes through u2 needing an extra step; the reward structure double-counts the exit condition across (u1→u2 at_exit 0.2) and (u2→u3 holding 1.0), making rewards not aligned with terminal payoff and giving +0.2 for a boxless exit. Summary: reject — the machine rewards exiting without the box (0.2), fails to enforce recovery after falls occurring in u2, and does not actually measure 'pick up on the very next move'. Rewrite so that any state after a fall requires holding_box within one step to re-arm, exit while holding is the only rewarded terminal, and exit while not holding yields no reward.
